title: Strong regular-functorial resolution of rig-regular formal varieties
statement: A Noetherian scheme means one with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. A Noetherian adic formal scheme is a ringed space admitting a finite open cover by spaces of the form $\operatorname{Spf}B$, the space of open prime ideals of a Noetherian ring $B$ complete and separated for powers of a finitely generated ideal, with its completed structure sheaf. Such a formal scheme is reduced when its affine chart rings are reduced. Quasi-excellence means quasi-excellence of its affine chart rings [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Regularity of a formal scheme means regularity of the rings on its formal affine charts [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Its singular locus is defined on $\operatorname{Spf}B$ by the radical ideal of the nonregular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. A formal blowup along a coherent ideal is obtained on each chart $\operatorname{Spf}B$ by taking the ordinary blowup of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ in the center ideal and then completing along the extended original ideal of definition [def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent]. A tower retains its ordered center ideals, including centers whose blowups happen to be isomorphisms. Consider all pairs $(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak I)$ over $\mathbf Q$ where $\mathfrak X$ is a reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent adic formal scheme, $\mathfrak I$ is an invertible ideal of definition, and $\mathfrak X$ is a finite disjoint union of formal varieties (its reduced closed fibres are of finite type over fields of characteristic zero [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Suppose it is rig-regular: the ideal $\mathfrak S$ defining its singular locus contains a power of $\mathfrak I$. A morphism $h:(\mathfrak Y,\mathfrak J)\to(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak I)$ satisfies $\mathfrak J=\mathfrak I\mathcal O_{\mathfrak Y}$ and is regular, meaning that on formal affine charts the induced homomorphisms are regular ring maps [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: flat, with every fibre ring Noetherian and regular after every finite extension of the residue field. There exists a single rule $\widehat F$ assigning to every such pair a finite tower of formal blowups with coherent open center ideals, nonempty regular centers lying over $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{sing}}$, and regular final formal scheme. For every such $h$, the tower $\widehat F(\mathfrak Y,\mathfrak J)$ is the formal pullback of $\widehat F(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak I)$ with precisely the empty centers removed, preserving every retained extended ideal and its order. The rule takes the empty formal scheme to the length-zero tower. Here open means containing a power of the extended ideal of definition at that level. No compatibility with changes of the distinguished ideal of definition is asserted.

proof.text: Fix the single rule $F_{\mathrm{Var}}$ from [lem-per-rig-variety-strong-resolution] on generically reduced varieties and finite disjoint unions. It is strong, compatible with ALL regular morphisms across arbitrary characteristic-zero fields, and its centers lie over the singular locus of the original input.

On a principal affine pair $(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak I)$ apply [lem-per-rig-principal-formal-algebraization] to obtain a reduced Elkik pair $(X,I)$ with this completion and $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subseteq V(I)$. Reduced implies generically reduced, so Step 1 applies. For a finite disjoint union of principal affines choose one such algebraization for each component and apply $F_{\mathrm{Var}}$ to their entire disjoint union, thereby fixing one common stage order.

Complete this algebraic tower, retaining its center ideals; this is the formal blowup tower supplied by [lem-per-rig-principal-formal-algebraization]. The centers lie over $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subseteq V(I)$ by [lem-per-rig-variety-strong-resolution]. On each Noetherian chart, set-theoretic support in $V(I)$ implies that a power of the principal ideal $I$ belongs to the center ideal. Thus the formal centers are open, and completing a center does not change it: its quotients by powers of $I$ are eventually constant. They remain regular and nonempty. To check singular support on the formal base, its algebraization rings are excellent by [lem-exc-fields-excellent] and [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], hence G-rings by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Their completion maps are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular]. At a point of a completed center, a regular local ring on the completed base would force the corresponding algebraic local ring to be regular by the flat local descent statement [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular], contradicting its membership in the original singular locus. Thus every completed center lies over $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{sing}}$.

source.place: §3.4.1 completion construction; §2.4.5 and §2.3.1; completion regularity also Stacks 0AH2 and descent 00OF

proof.text: The final algebraic level is a regular variety by Step 1. On each finite-type affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of that level, $A$ is excellent by [lem-exc-fields-excellent] and [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], so is a G-ring by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Its completion $\widehat A_I$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and $A\to\widehat A_I$ is flat with geometrically regular fibres by [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-map-ascent] to this regular source ring and Noetherian target: every fibre is regular, as required by that statement. Hence every resulting complete chart ring is regular, which is precisely regularity of the final formal level.

Apply [lem-per-rig-formal-resolution-intrinsic] to $F_{\mathrm{Var}}$, whose all-regular-morphisms hypothesis was fixed in Step 1. If two choices algebraize the same principal affine formal pair, the identity of their fixed completions identifies their completed ordered towers. For any regular morphism between principal affine completed pairs, use the node's completed-pair compatibility clause, which is deduced from its regular thick-fibre comparison with the loss of thickness $r$ and sufficiently large $n$. No map between the algebraizations or their fields is required. This yields a well-defined compatible rule on finite disjoint unions of principal affines, with exactly empty centers deleted and every retained ideal in order.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.5 and §3.4.1 intrinsic-dependence and regular-functoriality paragraphs

proof.text: Every object has a finite principal affine open cover: refine its finite formal affine cover by opens on which the invertible ideal is generated by one non-zero-divisor. Steps 2–5 define the input rule on finite disjoint unions of these charts, with their common stage order. Apply [lem-per-rig-formal-resolution-gluing] to obtain $\widehat F$ on all the stated pairs. The node glues the coherent open ideals and towers with their synchronization and preserves regularity, original-singular-locus support, and pullback compatibility. In particular any stated $h$ is a regular ideal-preserving formal morphism, so its source tower is the formal pullback target tower with exactly empty centers removed, retaining every other extended ideal in its order. The empty tower has length zero.
